questions.text: जब MnO2 को वायु की उपस्थिति में KOH के साथ संगलित किया जाता है, तो यह देता है :
questions.text_english: When MnO2 is fused with KOH in air, it gives :
questions.solution: When MnO2 is fused with KOH in the presence of air (oxygen acts as oxidising agent), the product formed is potassium manganate, K2MnO4. The reaction is: 2MnO2 + 4KOH + O2 → 2K2MnO4 + 2H2O. KMnO4 is not directly formed in this step; it requires further oxidation. Mn2O7 is an acidic oxide formed under different conditions, and Mn2O3 is not the product of this fusion reaction.

questions.text: लिगन्ड EDTA4− उदाहरण है :
questions.text_english: Ligand EDTA4− is an example of a :
questions.solution: EDTA4− (ethylenediaminetetraacetate) is a polydentate ligand because it has six donor atoms — two nitrogen atoms and four carboxylate oxygen atoms — that can simultaneously coordinate to a central metal ion. Monodentate ligands have only one donor atom, didentate have two, and tridentate have three, so options A, B, and C are incorrect.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित लिगन्ड में से कौन-सा कीलेट संकुल निर्मित करता है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following ligand forms chelate complex ?
questions.solution: Oxalate ion (C2O4^2−) is a bidentate ligand with two oxygen donor atoms that can bind simultaneously to the same central metal ion forming a ring structure called a chelate complex. Cl−, NO2−, and NH3 are monodentate ligands with only one donor atom each and therefore cannot form chelate rings.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से किसमें sp2 संकरित कार्बन X से आबंधित है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following contains sp2 hybridised carbon bonded to X ?
questions.image_description: Four structures shown: (A) CH2=CH-CH2-X (allylic position), (B) benzene ring with CH2-X group (benzylic), (C) CH2=CH-X (vinyl halide, sp2 carbon bonded to X), (D) CH3-CH2-X (sp3 carbon bonded to X)
questions.solution: In option C, CH2=CH−X, the carbon bearing X is part of a double bond and hence is sp2 hybridised. In option A, the X is on the allylic carbon (CH2) which is sp3. In option B, the X is on the CH2 group outside the ring, making that carbon sp3. In option D, X is attached to a saturated sp3 carbon. Therefore, only in C is X directly bonded to an sp2 carbon.
questions.topic: Hybridisation of carbon in organic halides

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा सर्वाधिक अम्लीय है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following is most acidic ?
questions.solution: p-Chlorophenol (option D) is the most acidic among the given compounds. The chlorine atom at the para position is an electron-withdrawing group that stabilises the phenoxide ion through inductive effect, making p-chlorophenol more acidic than phenol (B). Phenol itself is more acidic than benzyl alcohol (A) and cyclohexanol (C) due to resonance stabilisation of the phenoxide ion. Among phenols, the electron-withdrawing Cl group in option D increases acidity further.

questions.text: ऐनिसोल, HI के साथ अभिक्रिया करके देता है :
questions.text_english: Anisole reacts with HI to give :
questions.solution: When anisole (C6H5−O−CH3) reacts with HI, the cleavage of the C−O bond occurs at the less hindered side (the methyl side). The I− ion attacks the methyl group (the smaller alkyl group) via SN2 mechanism, producing phenol (C6H5OH) and methyl iodide (CH3I). The aryl−oxygen bond is not cleaved because aryl carbons resist SN2 attack. Hence option A is correct.

questions.text: एथेनॉल 413 K पर सांद्र H2SO4 के साथ गर्म करने पर देता है :
questions.text_english: Ethanol on heating with conc. H2SO4 at 413 K gives :
questions.solution: At 413 K (around 140°C), ethanol reacts with conc. H2SO4 to form diethyl ether (C2H5−O−C2H5) by intermolecular dehydration. However, at higher temperatures around 443 K (170°C), intramolecular dehydration occurs to give ethylene (CH2=CH2). Since the question states 413 K, the expected product is diethyl ether. But the correct answer marked in CBSE key is option D (CH2=CH2) — noting that at 413 K with excess acid and prolonged heating, elimination is favoured. The standard CBSE answer for this question is C2H5OC2H5 at 413 K. Re-examining: 413 K corresponds to ~140°C → diethyl ether. Therefore correct answer is C.

questions.text: दो द्रवों के स्थिरक्वाथी विलयन का क्वथनांक उन दोनों द्रवों के क्वथनांक से निम्नतर होता है जब यह :
questions.text_english: An azeotropic solution of two liquids has boiling point lower than either of them when it :

options.B: राउल्ट नियम से धनात्मक विचलन दर्शाता है
options.C: राउल्ट नियम से ऋणात्मक विचलन दर्शाता है
options.D: राउल्ट नियम से कोई विचलन नहीं दर्शाता है

options_english.B: shows positive deviation from Raoult's law
options_english.C: shows negative deviation from Raoult's law
options_english.D: shows no deviation from Raoult's law

questions.solution: A minimum boiling azeotrope has a boiling point lower than either of the pure components. This occurs when the solution shows positive deviation from Raoult's law, meaning the intermolecular forces between unlike molecules are weaker than those between like molecules, leading to higher vapour pressure and hence lower boiling point. Negative deviation leads to maximum boiling azeotrope with a boiling point higher than either pure component.

questions.text: किसी अवाष्पशील विलेय के जलीय विलयन के वाष्प दाब का आपेक्षिक अवनमन 0·0225 है। अवाष्पशील विलेय का मोल-अंश है :
questions.text_english: The relative lowering of vapour pressure of an aqueous solution containing non-volatile solute is 0·0225. The mole fraction of the non-volatile solute is :
questions.solution: By Raoult's law, the relative lowering of vapour pressure equals the mole fraction of the solute: (P° − P)/P° = x_solute. Since the relative lowering of vapour pressure is given as 0·0225, the mole fraction of the non-volatile solute is directly 0·0225. Therefore option D is correct.

questions.text: NaCl के जलीय विलयन के विद्युत-अपघटन के दौरान :
questions.text_english: During electrolysis of aqueous solution of NaCl :

options.A: कैथोड पर H2(g) मुक्त होती है
options.B: कैथोड पर Na निर्मित होता है
options.C: ऐनोड पर O2(g) मुक्त होती है
options.D: कैथोड पर Cl2(g) मुक्त होती है

questions.solution: During electrolysis of aqueous NaCl, at the cathode, reduction occurs. Water molecules are preferentially reduced over Na+ ions (since Na+ has a very negative reduction potential), producing H2(g) and OH− ions: 2H2O + 2e− → H2(g) + 2OH−. At the anode, Cl− ions are oxidised to Cl2(g). Na metal is not formed in aqueous solution, and O2 is not liberated at the anode under these conditions when concentrated NaCl is used.

questions.text: रासायनिक अभिक्रिया के दौरान उत्प्रेरक जोड़ने से अभिक्रिया की निम्नलिखित मात्राओं में से किसको परिवर्तित कर देता है ?
questions.text_english: The addition of catalyst during a chemical reaction alters which of the following quantities of the reaction ?
questions.solution: A catalyst works by providing an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy, thereby increasing the rate of reaction. It does not alter the enthalpy change (ΔH), entropy change (ΔS), or internal energy (ΔU) of the reaction, as these are thermodynamic state functions that depend only on initial and final states. Only the activation energy is altered by the catalyst.

questions.text: किसी प्राथमिक अभिक्रिया P→Q के लिए 'P' के लोप होने की दर, 'P' की सांद्रता दुगुनी करने पर, 8 के गुणक से बढ़ जाती है। 'P' के प्रति अभिक्रिया की कोटि है :
questions.text_english: For the elementary reaction P→Q, the rate of disappearance of 'P' increases by a factor of 8 upon doubling the concentration of 'P'. The order of the reaction with respect to 'P' is :
questions.solution: If the rate increases by a factor of 8 when the concentration of P is doubled, then 2^n = 8, where n is the order. Solving: 2^n = 8 = 2^3, so n = 3. The reaction is third order with respect to P. Options B (n=4 gives factor 16), C (n=2 gives factor 4), and D (n=1 gives factor 2) are all incorrect.

questions.text: ग्लूकोस (मोलर द्रव्यमान = 180 g mol−1) का 6% विलयन किसी अज्ञात कार्बनिक पदार्थ के 2·5% विलयन के साथ समपरासारी है। अज्ञात कार्बनिक पदार्थ का अणु भार परिकलित कीजिए।
questions.text_english: A 6% solution of glucose (molar mass = 180 g mol−1) is isotonic with 2·5% solution of an unknown organic substance. Calculate the molecular weight of the unknown organic substance.

key_points: Isotonic solutions have equal osmotic pressures, hence equal molar concentrations
Use: C1/M1 = C2/M2 where C is percentage and M is molar mass

questions.solution: Two isotonic solutions have the same osmotic pressure, which means they have the same molar concentration. For isotonic solutions: (w1/M1) = (w2/M2) per same volume, i.e., percentage/molar mass ratio is equal. Therefore, 6/180 = 2.5/M2. Solving: M2 = (2.5 × 180)/6 = 450/6 = 75 g mol−1. The molecular weight of the unknown organic substance is 75 g mol−1.

किसी प्रथम कोटि की अभिक्रिया का वेग स्थिरांक 1·25 × 10−3 s−1 है। इस अभिकर्मक के 5 g को 2·5 g में घटने में कितना समय लगेगा ?
[ log 2 = 0·301, log 3 = 0·4771, log 4 = 0·6021 ]
questions.text_english:
A first order reaction has a rate constant 1·25 × 10−3 s−1. How long will 5 g of this reactant take to reduce to 2·5 g ?
[ log 2 = 0·301, log 3 = 0·4771, log 4 = 0·6021 ]

key_points: Use first order formula: t = (2.303/k) × log(a/a-x)

questions.solution: For a first order reaction, t = (2.303/k) × log(a/(a−x)). Here, k = 1.25 × 10−3 s−1, initial amount a = 5 g, final amount (a−x) = 2.5 g. Therefore, t = (2.303 / 1.25 × 10−3) × log(5/2.5) = (2.303 / 1.25 × 10−3) × log 2 = 1842.4 × 0.301 ≈ 554.4 s. The reactant takes approximately 554.4 seconds to reduce from 5 g to 2.5 g.

(क) लैन्थेनॉयड आकुंचन क्या है ? लैन्थेनॉयड आकुंचन की तुलना में एक तत्व से दूसरे तत्व के बीच ऐक्टिनॉयड आकुंचन अधिक होता है। क्यों ?
अथवा
(ख) संक्रमण धातुएँ कणन एन्थैल्पी के उच्च मान क्यों दर्शाती हैं ? 3d-श्रेणी में किस तत्व की कणन एन्थैल्पी सबसे कम है ?
questions.text_english:
(a) What is lanthanoid contraction? Actinoid contraction is greater from element to element than lanthanoid contraction. Why ?
OR
(b) Why do transition metals have high enthalpy of atomization? Which element of 3d-series has lowest enthalpy of atomization?

key_points: Lanthanoid contraction: steady decrease in atomic/ionic radii across lanthanoids due to poor shielding by 4f electrons
Actinoid contraction is greater because 5f electrons provide even poorer shielding than 4f electrons
OR: Transition metals have high atomization enthalpy due to strong metallic bonding involving unpaired d-electrons
Zinc (Zn) has lowest enthalpy of atomization in 3d series because its d-subshell is completely filled (d10)

questions.solution: (a) Lanthanoid contraction is the gradual decrease in atomic and ionic radii of lanthanoid elements from La to Lu. This occurs because as atomic number increases, electrons are added to the inner 4f subshell, which provides poor shielding due to the diffuse nature of f orbitals. Actinoid contraction is greater from element to element than lanthanoid contraction because 5f electrons provide even poorer shielding of the nuclear charge than 4f electrons, resulting in a greater effective nuclear charge experienced by outer electrons. OR (b) Transition metals have high enthalpy of atomization because they form strong metallic bonds involving both s and d electrons. The presence of unpaired d-electrons allows for extensive metallic bonding, requiring large amounts of energy to separate atoms. Among the 3d series, zinc (Zn) has the lowest enthalpy of atomization because its 3d subshell is completely filled (3d10), meaning no d-electrons are available for metallic bonding, making the metallic bonding weaker.
questions.topic: Lanthanoid/Actinoid contraction; Atomization enthalpy of transition metals

(Neopentyl iodide OR neopentyl bromide — allyl iodide OR allyl bromide)
(b) Write the major product in the following :
Ethylbenzene + Cl2, UV light

key_points: Allyl iodide undergoes SN2 faster than allyl bromide because I is a better leaving group
For (b): Cl2/UV light on ethylbenzene causes free radical halogenation at the benzylic CH2 position giving 1-chloro-1-phenylethane (PhCHClCH3)

questions.solution: (a) Allyl iodide (CH2=CH−CH2−I) undergoes SN2 reaction faster than allyl bromide (CH2=CH−CH2−Br) because iodide (I−) is a better leaving group than bromide (Br−). The C−I bond is weaker and longer, making it easier to break. Both compounds have the same allylic position which is favourable for SN2, but the superior leaving group ability of iodide makes the iodide compound react faster. (b) When ethylbenzene reacts with Cl2 under UV light, free radical substitution occurs preferentially at the benzylic position (the carbon directly attached to the ring) to give 1-chloro-1-phenylethane (C6H5−CHCl−CH3) as the major product, since the benzylic radical formed is more stable due to resonance with the aromatic ring.

Define the following terms :
(a) Denaturation of protein
(b) Invert sugar

key_points: Denaturation: disruption of secondary and tertiary structure of protein by heat, acid or other agents, losing biological activity

Invert sugar: equimolar mixture of glucose and fructose obtained by hydrolysis of sucrose; called invert sugar because the optical rotation changes from dextrorotatory (+) sucrose to levorotatory (−) mixture

questions.solution: (a) Denaturation of protein refers to the process in which the secondary and tertiary structures of a protein are disrupted by physical agents (such as heat or UV radiation) or chemical agents (such as acids, bases, or organic solvents), without breaking the peptide bonds. The protein loses its biological activity as a result of the unfolding of its three-dimensional structure. (b) Invert sugar is the equimolar mixture of D-glucose and D-fructose obtained by the hydrolysis of sucrose. It is called invert sugar because sucrose is dextrorotatory (+66.5°) but after hydrolysis the resulting mixture is levorotatory (−19.8°), representing an inversion of the sign of optical rotation.

(ख) नाइट्रोबेंजीन → (Fe + HCl) → A → (NaNO2 + HCl, 273−278 K) → B → (C2H5OH) → C
questions.text_english:
Write the structures of A, B and C in the following reactions :
(a) CH3−CH2−Br → (KCN) → A → (Partial hydrolysis with OH−) → B → (NaOH + Br2) → C
(b) Nitrobenzene → (Fe + HCl) → A → (NaNO2 + HCl, 273−278 K) → B → (C2H5OH) → C

key_points: (a) A = CH3CH2CN (propionitrile), B = CH3CH2CONH2 (propionamide), C = CH3CH2NH2 (ethylamine/ethanamine)
(b) A = C6H5NH2 (aniline), B = C6H5N2+Cl− (benzene diazonium chloride), C = C6H5OC2H5 (ethoxybenzene/phenetole)

questions.solution: (a) CH3CH2Br reacts with KCN to give A = CH3CH2CN (propionitrile) via nucleophilic substitution. Partial hydrolysis of the nitrile with OH− gives B = CH3CH2CONH2 (propionamide). Treatment of propionamide with NaOH and Br2 (Hoffmann bromamide degradation) gives C = CH3CH2NH2 (ethanamine/ethylamine), which has one carbon fewer than the amide. (b) Nitrobenzene on reduction with Fe and HCl gives A = C6H5NH2 (aniline). Aniline reacts with NaNO2 and HCl at 273−278 K (diazotisation) to give B = C6H5N2+Cl− (benzene diazonium chloride). Treatment of the diazonium salt with C2H5OH gives C = C6H5OC2H5 (phenetole/ethoxybenzene) via the Williamson-type reaction where the diazonium group is replaced by the ethoxy group.

Write the reaction involved in the following :
(a) Wolff-Kishner reduction
(b) Decarboxylation reaction
(c) Cannizzaro reaction

key_points: Wolff-Kishner: aldehyde/ketone + N2H4 + KOH/ethylene glycol/heat → alkane + N2
Decarboxylation: RCOONa + NaOH → RH + Na2CO3 (heating)
Cannizzaro: 2HCHO + NaOH → CH3OH + HCOONa (disproportionation of non-enolisable aldehydes)

questions.solution: (a) Wolff-Kishner reduction: A carbonyl compound (aldehyde or ketone) is treated with hydrazine (N2H4) in the presence of a base such as KOH in ethylene glycol at high temperature. The carbonyl group (C=O) is completely reduced to a −CH2− group with the evolution of nitrogen gas. For example: CH3CHO + N2H4 → CH3CH=N−NH2 → CH3CH3 + N2 (in presence of KOH/heat). (b) Decarboxylation: When sodium salt of a carboxylic acid (RCOONa) is heated with soda lime (NaOH + CaO), carbon dioxide is lost and an alkane is formed. For example: CH3COONa + NaOH → CH4 + Na2CO3. (c) Cannizzaro reaction: Aldehydes that do not have an alpha hydrogen atom undergo self-oxidation-reduction (disproportionation) in the presence of concentrated NaOH. One molecule of aldehyde is oxidised to the carboxylate salt while another is reduced to the alcohol. For example: 2HCHO + NaOH → CH3OH + HCOONa.

Give the equations of reactions for the preparation of : (any three)
(a) Phenol from chlorobenzene
(b) Salicylaldehyde from phenol
(c) 2-Methoxyacetophenone from anisole
(d) Picric acid from phenol

key_points: (a) C6H5Cl + NaOH(aq) → C6H5ONa + HCl (high temp/pressure), then C6H5ONa + HCl → C6H5OH + NaCl
(b) Phenol + CHCl3 + NaOH (Reimer-Tiemann) → 2-hydroxybenzaldehyde (salicylaldehyde)
(c) Anisole + CH3COCl/AlCl3 (Friedel-Crafts acylation, ortho attack) → 2-methoxyacetophenone
(d) Phenol + conc. HNO3 + conc. H2SO4 (nitration, excess) → 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (picric acid)

questions.solution: (a) Phenol from chlorobenzene: Chlorobenzene is heated with aqueous NaOH at 623 K and 300 atm pressure (Dow process). C6H5Cl + NaOH(aq) → C6H5ONa + HCl; then C6H5ONa + HCl → C6H5OH + NaCl. (b) Salicylaldehyde from phenol: Phenol reacts with chloroform (CHCl3) in the presence of aqueous KOH (Reimer-Tiemann reaction). The electrophilic CHCl2+ species attacks the ortho position of phenoxide to give salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde). C6H5OH + CHCl3 + KOH → 2-HO-C6H4-CHO + 3KCl + H2O. (c) 2-Methoxyacetophenone from anisole: Anisole undergoes Friedel-Crafts acylation with acetyl chloride (CH3COCl) in the presence of anhydrous AlCl3. The −OCH3 group directs the incoming acyl group to the ortho position, giving 2-methoxyacetophenone. C6H5OCH3 + CH3COCl → 2-CH3O-C6H4-COCH3 + HCl (AlCl3 catalyst). (d) Picric acid from phenol: Phenol is first treated with dilute HNO3 to give o- and p-nitrophenol, and then treated with concentrated HNO3/H2SO4 (mixed acid) to give 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (picric acid).

questions.text_english:
Give reasons for the following :
(a) Chlorine is ortho/para directing in electrophilic aromatic substitution reactions, though chlorine is an electron withdrawing group.
(b) Racemic mixture is optically inactive.
(c) Allyl chloride is hydrolysed more readily than n-propyl chloride.

key_points: (a) Cl has lone pairs that donate electrons to ring by resonance, activating ortho/para positions despite being -I group
(b) Racemic mixture has equal amounts of d and l forms; their optical rotations cancel each other
(c) Allyl chloride forms stabilised allylic carbocation intermediate; resonance stabilisation makes it easier to hydrolyse

questions.solution: (a) Chlorine is an electron-withdrawing group by the inductive effect (−I), which would deactivate the ring. However, chlorine has three lone pairs on it that can donate electrons into the benzene ring through resonance (+M effect), making the ortho and para positions electron-rich. Since the resonance effect (+M) dominates over the inductive effect (−I) in directing the incoming electrophile, chlorine acts as an ortho/para director, although the ring is overall deactivated compared to benzene. (b) A racemic mixture contains equal amounts of the d-form (dextrorotatory) and l-form (levorotatory) of a chiral compound. The clockwise rotation due to the d-enantiomer is exactly cancelled by the anticlockwise rotation due to the l-enantiomer, resulting in a net zero optical rotation. Hence the racemic mixture is optically inactive. (c) Allyl chloride (CH2=CH−CH2Cl) is hydrolysed more readily than n-propyl chloride because on ionisation it forms an allylic carbocation (CH2=CH−CH2+) which is stabilised by resonance involving the adjacent double bond. The resonance-stabilised intermediate lowers the activation energy of the reaction, making hydrolysis faster compared to n-propyl chloride which gives an unstable primary carbocation with no resonance stabilisation.

questions.text: 283 K पर किसी विलायक का वाष्प दाब 100 mm Hg है। उस तनु विलयन का वाष्प दाब परिकलित कीजिए जिसमें 283 K पर किसी प्रबल विद्युत-अपघट्य AB का 1 मोल विलायक के 50 मोल में घुला है (यह मान लीजिए कि विलेय AB पूर्णतः वियोजित हो जाता है)।
questions.text_english: The vapour pressure of a solvent at 283 K is 100 mm Hg. Calculate the vapour pressure of a dilute solution containing 1 mole of a strong electrolyte AB in 50 moles of the solvent at 283 K (assuming complete dissociation of solute AB).

key_points: AB dissociates completely into A+ and B−, giving i=2, so effective moles of solute = 2
Mole fraction of solvent = 50/(50+2) = 50/52
Vapour pressure of solution = mole fraction of solvent × P° = (50/52) × 100 = 96.15 mm Hg

questions.solution: Since AB is a strong electrolyte and completely dissociates, AB → A+ + B−. So 1 mole of AB gives 2 moles of ions. Total moles of solute particles = 2. Moles of solvent = 50. By Raoult's law: P = x_solvent × P° where x_solvent = n_solvent/(n_solvent + n_solute) = 50/(50 + 2) = 50/52. Therefore, P = (50/52) × 100 = 5000/52 ≈ 96.15 mm Hg. The vapour pressure of the solution is approximately 96.15 mm Hg.

[ log 10 = 1 ]
questions.text_english:
Calculate emf of the following cell :
Zn(s) | Zn2+(0·1 M) || Sn2+(0·001 M) | Sn(s)
Given : E°Zn2+/Zn = −0·76 V, E°Sn2+/Sn = −0·14 V
[ log 10 = 1 ]

key_points: E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode = −0.14 − (−0.76) = +0.62 V
Nernst equation: Ecell = E°cell − (0.0591/n) × log Q

questions.solution: The cell reaction: Zn(s) → Zn2+(aq) + 2e− (oxidation at anode); Sn2+(aq) + 2e− → Sn(s) (reduction at cathode). E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode = −0.14 − (−0.76) = +0.62 V. Using the Nernst equation: Ecell = E°cell − (0.0591/n) × log([Zn2+]/[Sn2+]) where n = 2. Q = [Zn2+]/[Sn2+] = 0.1/0.001 = 100. Ecell = 0.62 − (0.0591/2) × log 100 = 0.62 − (0.0591/2) × 2 = 0.62 − 0.0591 = 0.5609 V ≈ 0.56 V. The emf of the cell is approximately 0.56 V.

questions.text:
ताप में 17°C से 27°C तक वृद्धि करने पर किसी गैसीय अभिक्रिया का वेग तीन गुना हो जाता है। इस अभिक्रिया के लिए सक्रियण ऊर्जा का परिकलन कीजिए।
[ दिया गया है : 2·303 R = 19·15 JK−1 mol−1, log 3 = 0·48 ]
questions.text_english:
The rate of a gaseous reaction triples when temperature is increased from 17°C to 27°C. Calculate the energy of activation for this reaction.
[Given : 2·303 R = 19·15 JK−1 mol−1, log 3 = 0·48]
questions.solution: T1 = 17°C + 273 = 290 K; T2 = 27°C + 273 = 300 K; k2/k1 = 3. Using the Arrhenius equation: log(k2/k1) = Ea/(2.303R) × (T2 − T1)/(T1 × T2). Substituting: log 3 = Ea/19.15 × (300 − 290)/(290 × 300) = Ea/19.15 × 10/87000. 0.48 = Ea × 10/(19.15 × 87000). Ea = 0.48 × 19.15 × 87000/10 = 0.48 × 166605 = 79970.4 J mol−1 ≈ 80 kJ mol−1. The activation energy for the reaction is approximately 80 kJ mol−1.

questions.text: कार्बोहाइड्रेट पौधों और प्राणियों दोनों में जीवन के लिए आवश्यक होते हैं। पौधों में स्टार्च की तरह और प्राणियों में ग्लाइकोजन के रूप में कार्बोहाइड्रेट संग्रहण अणुओं की भाँति प्रयुक्त होते हैं। रासायनिक रूप से ये पॉलिहाइड्रॉक्सी ऐल्डिहाइड अथवा कीटोन होते हैं। कार्बोहाइड्रेटों को जल-अपघटन में उनके व्यवहार के आधार पर मोनोसैकैराइड, ओलिगोसैकैराइड और पॉलिसैकैराइड में वर्गीकृत किया गया है। सभी मोनोसैकैराइड अपचायी शर्करा होती हैं, अर्थात् ये टॉलेन अभिकर्मक तथा फेलिंग विलयन से ऑक्सीकृत हो जाती हैं। ग्लूकोस जैसा मोनोसैकैराइड एल्डोहैक्सोज होता है और इसका आण्विक सूत्र C6H12O6 पाया गया। विभिन्न अभिकर्मकों जैसे HI, H2N-OH, ब्रोमीन जल, (CH3CO)2O इत्यादि के साथ अभिक्रिया करके इसकी संरचना में एक ऐल्डिहाइड समूह, एक प्राथमिक ऐल्कोहॉलिक समूह (-CH2OH) और चार द्वितीयक ऐल्कोहॉलिक समूह (>CHOH) पाए गए। ऐल्डिहाइड समूह उपस्थित होते हुए भी ग्लूकोस ऐल्डिहाइड समूह की कुछ अभिक्रियाएँ जैसे शिफ परीक्षण, NaHSO3 योगज नहीं देता है। यह ग्लूकोस के दो चक्रीय हैमीऐसीटैल रूपों के अस्तित्व को समझाता है जिनमें भिन्नता केवल C-1 पर उपस्थित हाइड्रॉक्सिल समूह के विन्यास में होती है।
questions.text_english: Carbohydrates are essential for life in both plants and animals. Carbohydrates are used as storage molecules as starch in plants and glycogen in animals. Chemically they are polyhydroxy aldehydes or ketones. On the basis of their behaviour on hydrolysis, carbohydrates are classified as monosaccharides, oligosaccharides and polysaccharides. All monosaccharides are reducing sugars, i.e., they are oxidized by Tollens' reagent and Fehling's solution. A monosaccharide like glucose is aldohexose and its molecular formula was found to be C6H12O6. After reacting with different reagents like HI, H2N−OH, Bromine water, (CH3CO)2O, etc. its structure was found to contain one aldehyde group, one primary alcoholic group, (−CH2OH) and four secondary alcoholic groups (>CHOH). Despite having the aldehyde group, glucose does not give some of the reactions of aldehyde group like Schiff's test, NaHSO3 addition. This explains the existence of glucose in two cyclic hemiacetal forms which differ only in the configuration of the hydroxyl group at C−1.

key_points: Sugars that can reduce Tollens' reagent (ammoniacal silver nitrate) and Fehling's solution
They have a free aldehyde or ketone group that acts as a reducing agent

sub_questions.solution: Reducing sugars are carbohydrates that can reduce Tollens' reagent and Fehling's solution. Examples include glucose, fructose, maltose, and lactose.

sub_questions.solution: Glycogen is the polysaccharide known as 'animal starch'. questions.text: संक्रमण धातुओं के उदासीन परमाणु अथवा आयन में d-कक्षक अपूर्ण होते हैं। इनके परमाणुओं में आंशिक भरित d-कक्षकों की उपस्थिति संक्रमण तत्वों को असंक्रमण तत्वों से अलग कर देती है। आंशिक रूप से भरित d-कक्षकों के कारण ये तत्व कुछ अभिलक्षणिक गुण दर्शाते हैं, जैसे अनेक ऑक्सीकरण अवस्थाएँ, रंगीन आयनों का बनना तथा अनेक प्रकार के लिगन्डों के साथ संकुल निर्माण आदि। संक्रमण धातुएँ तथा इनके यौगिक उत्प्रेरकी गुण व अनुचुम्बकीय व्यवहार भी दर्शाते हैं। संक्रमण धातुएँ अति कठोर तथा अल्प वाष्पशील होती हैं। इनके E°M2+/M के मानों की जाँच परिवर्ती प्रवृत्ति दर्शाती है।

Zn in +2 state has configuration [Ar] 3d10, with completely filled d-subshell, so it is not a transition element

sub_questions.solution: Copper (Cu, Z=29) has the electronic configuration [Ar] 3d10 4s1 in the ground state. In its +2 oxidation state (Cu2+), its configuration becomes [Ar] 3d9, which has an incompletely filled d-subshell. Since a transition element is defined as one which has partially filled d-orbitals in its ground state or in any of its common oxidation states, Cu qualifies as a transition element. Zinc (Zn, Z=30) has the configuration [Ar] 3d10 4s2 and its +2 ion Zn2+ has [Ar] 3d10, which is a completely filled d-subshell. Since Zn never has a partially filled d-subshell in any oxidation state, it is not considered a transition element.

sub_questions.text_english: Why do transition elements show variety of oxidation states ?

key_points: 3d and 4s electrons have comparable energies and can be lost in varying numbers
This allows transition metals to exhibit multiple oxidation states

sub_questions.solution: Transition elements show a variety of oxidation states because the energies of the 3d and 4s orbitals are very close to each other. As a result, electrons from both the 3d and 4s orbitals can be involved in bonding. Different numbers of electrons can be lost from these orbitals depending on the chemical environment, giving rise to multiple oxidation states ranging from +2 (by losing the two 4s electrons) up to the maximum state equal to the number of 3d and 4s electrons combined.

sub_questions.text_english: How is the crystal field splitting energy for octahedral complex (Δo) related to that of tetrahedral complex (Δt) ?

key_points: Δt = (4/9) Δo

sub_questions.solution: The crystal field splitting energy for a tetrahedral complex (Δt) is related to that of an octahedral complex (Δo) by the relationship: Δt = (4/9)Δo. This means the splitting in tetrahedral complexes is smaller than in octahedral complexes for the same metal ion and same set of ligands, primarily because in tetrahedral complexes none of the ligands point directly towards any d-orbital, resulting in weaker interaction.

key_points: Dichloridobis(ethane-1,2-diamine)platinum(IV) nitrate

sub_questions.solution: The IUPAC name of [PtCl2(en)2](NO3)2 is dichloridobis(ethane-1,2-diamine)platinum(IV) nitrate. The central metal is Pt in +4 oxidation state (since 2 Cl each −1 and 2 NO3− outside give charge balance: +4 − 2 = +2 overall for complex cation with 2 NO3−, confirming Pt is +4). sub_questions.text_english: Write the geometry and magnetic behaviour of the complex [Ni(CO)4] on the basis of Valency Bond Theory (VBT).

key_points: Ni in [Ni(CO)4] is in 0 oxidation state with 3d10 configuration
CO causes pairing and sp3 hybridisation — tetrahedral geometry
All electrons are paired — diamagnetic

sub_questions.solution: In [Ni(CO)4], nickel is in the 0 oxidation state with the electronic configuration [Ar] 3d10. CO is a strong field ligand and causes the electrons to pair up. Since all 10 d-electrons are already paired in the d10 configuration, Ni uses sp3 hybridisation (using one 4s and three 4p orbitals) to accommodate the four CO ligands. The geometry is tetrahedral. Since all electrons are paired, the complex is diamagnetic.

sub_questions.text: संकुल [Co(NH3)6][Cr(CN)6] के द्वारा किस प्रकार की समावयवता दर्शाई जाती है ?
sub_questions.text_english: What type of isomerism is shown by the complex [Co(NH3)6][Cr(CN)6] ?

key_points: Coordination isomerism

sub_questions.solution: The complex [Co(NH3)6][Cr(CN)6] shows coordination isomerism. In this type of isomerism, the ligands are exchanged between the cationic and anionic complex units. Its coordination isomer is [Cr(NH3)6][Co(CN)6], in which the NH3 ligands have moved to chromium and the CN− ligands have moved to cobalt. Coordination isomerism occurs only in compounds containing both a complex cation and a complex anion.

sub_questions.text: क्रिस्टल क्षेत्र सिद्धांत के आधार पर किसी उपसहसंयोजन यौगिक में d4 आयन का इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास लिखिए यदि Δo < P हो। क्या यह उपसहसंयोजन यौगिक उच्च प्रचक्रण अथवा निम्न प्रचक्रण संकुल है ?
sub_questions.text_english: For the coordination compound on the basis of crystal field theory, write the electronic configuration for d4 ion if Δo < P. Is the coordination compound a high spin or low spin complex ?

key_points: When Δo < P (pairing energy), electrons occupy higher energy eg orbitals rather than pairing in t2g
Configuration: t2g3 eg1
This is a high spin complex

sub_questions.solution: When Δo < P (crystal field splitting energy is less than pairing energy), it is energetically more favourable for electrons to occupy the higher energy eg orbitals rather than to pair up in the t2g orbitals. For a d4 ion in an octahedral field with Δo < P, the electronic configuration is t2g3 eg1 (one electron in each of the three t2g and one in eg, all unpaired). This gives 4 unpaired electrons and is a high spin complex.

sub_questions.text: [Co(NH3)6]3+ और [Co(NH3)4Cl2]+ में से कौन हेट्रोलेप्टिक संकुल है और क्यों ?
sub_questions.text_english: Out of [Co(NH3)6]3+ and [Co(NH3)4Cl2]+, which complex is heteroleptic and why ?

key_points: [Co(NH3)4Cl2]+ is heteroleptic because it contains two different types of ligands (NH3 and Cl−)
[Co(NH3)6]3+ is homoleptic as it contains only one type of ligand (NH3)

sub_questions.solution: [Co(NH3)4Cl2]+ is the heteroleptic complex because it contains two different types of ligands — ammonia (NH3) and chloride (Cl−). A heteroleptic complex is one that has more than one kind of ligand coordinated to the central metal ion. In contrast, [Co(NH3)6]3+ is homoleptic because it contains only one type of ligand, which is NH3, bound to the cobalt centre.

The cis isomer is chiral and exists as d and l forms (optical isomers)
The trans isomer has a plane of symmetry and is optically inactive

sub_questions.solution: [PtCl2(en)2]2+ in the cis configuration has no plane of symmetry and is chiral, therefore it exists as two non-superimposable mirror images (optical isomers): the d-form (dextrorotatory) and the l-form (levorotatory). questions.text_english:
(a) (i) Account for the following :
(1) Oxidation of aldehydes is easier as compared to ketones.
(2) The alpha (α) hydrogen atoms of aldehydes are acidic in nature.
(ii) Write the products in the following reactions :
(1) Acetophenone + NaOH/I2 →
(2) Benzoyl chloride + (CH3)2Cd →
(iii) Give a simple chemical test to distinguish between ethanoic acid and ethanal.
OR
(b) (i) Draw structure of the 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazone of benzaldehyde.
(ii) Arrange the following in increasing order of their reactivity towards HCN : CH3COCH3, (CH3)3C−COCH3, CH3CHO
(iii) How can you convert phenyl magnesium bromide to benzoic acid ?
(iv) Give a simple chemical test to distinguish between benzaldehyde and ethanal.
(v) Write the main product in the following reaction : CH3−CO−CH2−COOC2H5 → (i) NaBH4, (ii) H+

key_points: (a)(i)(1): Aldehydes have H on carbonyl carbon making it easier to oxidise; ketones lack this H
(a)(i)(2): Alpha H in aldehydes is acidic due to electron-withdrawing effect of C=O making the adjacent C−H more polarised
(a)(ii)(1): Acetophenone + NaOH/I2 → CHI3 (iodoform) + sodium benzoate (C6H5COONa)
(a)(ii)(2): C6H5COCl + (CH3)2Cd → C6H5COCH3 (acetophenone) + CdCl2
(a)(iii): Ethanoic acid turns blue litmus red and effervesces with Na2CO3; ethanal gives silver mirror with Tollens' reagent
OR answers provided below

questions.solution: (a)(i)(1) Aldehydes are more easily oxidised than ketones because the carbonyl carbon in an aldehyde has a hydrogen atom directly attached to it (−CHO). This hydrogen is available for abstraction during oxidation. In ketones, the carbonyl carbon has two alkyl/aryl groups instead of a hydrogen, making oxidation much harder as a C−C bond would need to be broken. (a)(i)(2) The alpha (α) hydrogen atoms in aldehydes are acidic because the electron-withdrawing carbonyl group (C=O) adjacent to the alpha carbon increases the polarity of the C−H bond at the alpha position. Furthermore, the resulting carbanion (enolate) is stabilised by resonance with the carbonyl group. (a)(ii)(1) Acetophenone (C6H5COCH3) has an −COCH3 group and undergoes the iodoform reaction with NaOH/I2 to give iodoform (CHI3) and sodium benzoate (C6H5COONa): C6H5COCH3 + 3I2 + 4NaOH → CHI3 + C6H5COONa + 3NaI + 3H2O. (a)(ii)(2) Benzoyl chloride (C6H5COCl) reacts with dimethylcadmium [(CH3)2Cd] in a Cadmium-based Grignard-type reaction to give acetophenone (C6H5COCH3) + CdCl2: 2C6H5COCl + (CH3)2Cd → 2C6H5COCH3 + CdCl2. (a)(iii) To distinguish ethanoic acid from ethanal: Add sodium carbonate (Na2CO3) solution — ethanoic acid effervesces with CO2 gas (CH3COOH + Na2CO3 → CH3COONa + CO2 + H2O), while ethanal does not. Alternatively, add Tollens' reagent — ethanal gives a silver mirror (positive test) while ethanoic acid does not. OR (b)(i) The 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazone of benzaldehyde is formed by the reaction of benzaldehyde (C6H5CHO) with 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine. Its structure is: C6H5−CH=N−NH−C6H3(NO2)2, a yellow/orange precipitate with the double bond between C and N. (b)(ii) Reactivity towards HCN (nucleophilic addition) increases with the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon and decreases with steric hindrance. Increasing order: (CH3)3C−COCH3 < CH3COCH3 < CH3CHO. Explanation: CH3CHO is most reactive (least hindered, more electrophilic); (CH3)3C−COCH3 is least reactive (most sterically hindered). (b)(iii) Phenyl magnesium bromide (C6H5MgBr) is converted to benzoic acid by reacting it with CO2 (dry ice) followed by hydrolysis: C6H5MgBr + CO2 → C6H5COOMgBr; then C6H5COOMgBr + H2O → C6H5COOH + Mg(OH)Br. (b)(iv) To distinguish benzaldehyde from ethanal: Use iodoform test — ethanal gives a yellow precipitate of iodoform (CHI3) with NaOH and I2, while benzaldehyde does not (it lacks the −COCH3 or −CH(OH)CH3 group). Alternatively, use Fehling's solution — ethanal reduces Fehling's solution to give a brick-red precipitate of Cu2O, while benzaldehyde does not. (b)(v) CH3−CO−CH2−COOC2H5 (ethyl acetoacetate) treated with (i) NaBH4 then (ii) H+: NaBH4 selectively reduces the ketone (C=O) group without affecting the ester group. The main product is CH3−CH(OH)−CH2−COOC2H5 (ethyl 3-hydroxybutanoate).

(a) (i) The resistance of 0·05 M CH3COOH solution is found to be 100 ohm. If the cell constant is 0·0354 cm−1, calculate the molar conductivity of the acetic acid solution.
(ii) State Faraday's first law of electrolysis. How much charge in Faraday is required for the reduction of 1 mol of MnO4− to Mn2+ ?
OR
(b) (i) The conductivity of 0·0025 mol L−1 acetic acid is 5·25 × 10−5 S cm−1. Calculate its degree of dissociation if Λ°m for acetic acid is 390 S cm2 mol−1.
(ii) Write anode, cathode and overall reaction of lead storage battery.

key_points: (a)(ii): Faraday's first law: mass deposited ∝ charge passed; MnO4− + 8H+ + 5e− → Mn2+ + 4H2O; 5 Faraday per mole
(b)(ii): Anode: Pb + SO42− → PbSO4 + 2e−; Cathode: PbO2 + 4H+ + SO42− + 2e− → PbSO4 + 2H2O; Overall: Pb + PbO2 + 2H2SO4 → 2PbSO4 + 2H2O

questions.solution: (a)(i) Conductivity (κ) = Cell constant / Resistance = 0.0354 cm−1 / 100 Ω = 3.54 × 10−4 S cm−1. Molar conductivity Λm = (κ × 1000) / Molarity = (3.54 × 10−4 × 1000) / 0.05 = 0.354/0.05 = 7.08 S cm2 mol−1. (a)(ii) Faraday's first law of electrolysis: The mass of substance deposited or dissolved at an electrode during electrolysis is directly proportional to the quantity of electricity (charge) passed through the electrolyte. The reduction of MnO4− to Mn2+ involves a change in oxidation state from +7 to +2, a change of 5. So 5 moles of electrons (5 Faraday of charge) are required per mole of MnO4−: MnO4− + 8H+ + 5e− → Mn2+ + 4H2O. Therefore 5 Faraday of charge is required. OR (b)(i) Λm = (κ × 1000) / c = (5.25 × 10−5 × 1000) / 0.0025 = 0.0525/0.0025 = 21 S cm2 mol−1. Degree of dissociation α = Λm / Λ°m = 21/390 = 0.0538 ≈ 5.38%. (b)(ii) Lead storage battery reactions: Anode (oxidation): Pb(s) + SO42−(aq) → PbSO4(s) + 2e−. Cathode (reduction): PbO2(s) + 4H+(aq) + SO42−(aq) + 2e− → PbSO4(s) + 2H2O(l). Overall: Pb(s) + PbO2(s) + 2H2SO4(aq) → 2PbSO4(s) + 2H2O(l).
